rv.q: It is a long time since I left a theatre feeling as I did after seeing Machinal.

It is a masterclass in how to play a character at the end of her tether. Sheehy is matched with a stellar supporting cast: Tim Frances does well to make her husband seem a warm and avuncular figure yet, at the same time, clearly bad news for her while Pierro Niel-Mee excels at making her lover – the Young Man – a slightly slippery charmer.
It's not without longueurs, yet it's a show that keeps humming in your head long after the final blackout.
It's theatrical torture that does to the viewer what the State of New York did to our poor, deluded heroine.
You rarely see such meticulous, detailed work in the theatre.
